body:
Global crypto markets are holding a fragile equilibrium this Sunday, with total market cap sitting at $2.3T, up just 0.06% over the past 24 hours. Volume across the space came in at $31.9B, a figure that suggests conviction remains thin and participants are broadly in wait-and-see mode. The Fear and Greed index ticked up a single point to 31, still firmly in Fear territory and only marginally improved from yesterday's 30. BTC dominance at 56.6% and ETH dominance at 10.1% paint a picture of capital hugging the largest asset while the broader altcoin complex struggles to generate sustained interest. The mood is cautious but not panicked — a market that is consolidating rather than capitulating.

Bitcoin is trading at $64,786, essentially flat over 24 hours at -0.20% but constructive on the weekly at +2.20%. The 1-hour chart is showing a marginal +0.10% nudge, which is consistent with low-velocity weekend price action rather than any directional commitment. Volume at $12.13B is respectable but not the kind of number that signals institutional aggression. The more significant narrative around BTC today is the BIP-110 soft fork drama: according to CoinDesk and Cointelegraph, the controversial fork mined 2 blocks before stalling, with miner support reportedly below 3% as mandatory signaling begins at block 961,632. This is a technical distraction more than a systemic threat, but it introduces a layer of protocol-level noise that traders should monitor. On the constructive side, US spot Bitcoin ETFs posted their best week since April with $1B in inflows per Cointelegraph, a number that adds meaningful support to the longer-term bid.

Solana is the standout in today's altcoin tape, up 2.30% over 24 hours to $76.2 with $1.25B in volume — the strongest combination of price performance and liquidity among tracked majors. BNB gained 1.70% to $602.65 and LINK added 0.90% to $8.33, rounding out the top 3 performers. On the other side, UNI is the session's clearest laggard at -1.40% to $3.97, extending its 7-day decline to -4.80%, which is a notable underperformance relative to the rest of the DeFi complex. ADA shed 1.10% to $0.198756 despite its impressive 7-day gain of +6.60%, suggesting some short-term profit-taking is now arriving. XRP at $1.036 is +0.70% on the day but is nursing a 7-day loss of -3.90%, a divergence worth watching given how closely the asset tracks regulatory headlines. AVAX at $6.47 is also struggling on both the 24-hour (-0.60%) and 7-day (-1.80%) timeframes, putting it in the same bracket as UNI as a relative underperformer this cycle.

The macro backdrop is doing more work than the charts. Brazil's central bank has ordered exchanges to delay large crypto transfers abroad per CoinDesk, a move that signals tightening regulatory posture in one of the hemisphere's largest markets and is consistent with the broader global trend of authorities moving to corral cross-border crypto flows. In Russia, hardware wallet sales have more than doubled as new crypto rules approach, per CoinDesk — a data point that speaks to retail-level demand driven by regulatory pressure rather than price enthusiasm. On the US legislative front, Cointelegraph reports Senate Majority Leader Thune has filed cloture to advance the CLARITY Act, with a vote expected in September, which is a meaningful step toward the kind of structural regulatory clarity that institutional allocators have been waiting for. Bitwise's Matt Hougan is quoted by CoinDesk suggesting trillions in institutional money are positioned to flow into Bitcoin — that narrative gains credibility if the CLARITY Act moves forward. The BTCPay Lightning vulnerability reported by Cointelegraph, where attackers stole funds via remote access, is a reminder that infrastructure risk remains live even as institutional interest grows.

Watch the BIP-110 signaling window closely — if miner support stays below 3%, this story fades quickly, but any unexpected surge in hash rate support would introduce real protocol uncertainty and could weigh on BTC price. The CLARITY Act cloture vote in September is the most significant medium-term catalyst in this data set; a procedural failure there would likely compress risk appetite across the space. SOL needs to hold above $76 to consolidate today's gains and confirm a higher low on the weekly structure. For the broader market, a sustained Fear and Greed reading below 30 would signal deteriorating sentiment that could pressure the $2.3T market cap floor. The $1B ETF inflow figure from last week is the cleanest bullish data point in the current setup — if that pace holds into next week's flow data, it changes the narrative materially.
